topStories.headline: Hales Leads Sheriff Race, Republicans Win Most County Contests in Preliminary Results
topStories.dek: Wasatch County Emergency Manager Jeremy Hales holds a commanding lead in the sheriff's race, while Republicans lead across most county offices in unofficial November 3 results.
topStories.body:
Wasatch County voters turned out in force on November 3, with more than 14,600 ballots received by election day, touching contests from sheriff and county attorney to state legislative seats. In the most-watched local race, Emergency Management Director Jeremy Hales — who beat incumbent Sheriff Jared Rigby in June's Republican primary by a 2-to-1 margin — led unaffiliated challenger Paul Moore nearly 69% to 32% in unofficial tallies as of Wednesday morning.

In the three Wasatch County Council races, Republicans Rachel Kahler, Erik Rowland, and Michael Murphy led their opponents in preliminary results. Kahler, executive director of the Community Alliance for Main Street and a former Heber City councilmember, held about 55% of the vote in the at-large Seat A contest against Democrat Robert McNeill. The Seat F race was tightest: incumbent Councilmember Murphy led Democrat Joe Tugaw by roughly 140 votes, with the district covering Hideout, Timber Lakes, and eastern Wasatch County.

In State House District 59, which spans multiple counties, Democrat Celeste T. Johnson held a razor-thin overall lead of about 50.1% to Republican Luke Searle's 49.9% in unofficial statewide results — but Searle dominated within Wasatch County itself, pulling 54.6% of local ballots. County deputy attorney John Woodard led Democrat Lauren Forsyth in the county attorney race.

All results remain unofficial until the County Council certifies the canvass, which is expected in approximately two weeks.

topStories.headline: Cyberattack Prompts Heber City to Overhaul Its IT Contract
topStories.dek: Following an October breach of municipal computer systems, the Heber City Council unanimously approved a new, more expensive technology agreement aimed at preventing future intrusions.
topStories.body:
The Heber City Council voted unanimously on November 3 to replace its decade-old information technology contract after city systems were hit by a cyberattack last month. The new agreement with Executech will cover more secure email infrastructure and unlimited tech support — a significant departure from the previous deal, which capped service at 30 hours per month and charged $150 for each additional hour.

The upgraded contract will cost the city $174,000 annually, nearly doubling the $88,000 Heber currently pays. City prosecutor Mark Smedley told the council the new agreement is designed to reduce future risk, noting that most network breaches originate with human error — an employee clicking something that opens a pathway into city systems. The contract includes mandatory employee cybersecurity training to address that vulnerability.

Councilmember Aaron Cheatwood raised concerns about the fiscal impact on Heber residents, though the motion ultimately passed without opposition. City officials did not publicly describe the full scope of the October breach or whether any sensitive data was compromised.

topStories.headline: Wasatch County School Enrollment Keeps Falling; District Opens Seats to Out-of-Boundary Students
topStories.dek: Wasatch County School District has shed more than 200 students since 2025, and its Board of Education has responded by opening enrollment to families from outside district boundaries for the 2027-28 school year.
topStories.body:
Wasatch County School District enrolled 6,822 students this fall, a loss of more than 200 since 2025, according to figures reported November 5 by KPCW. The decline follows a statewide trend affecting most districts along the Wasatch Back and comes despite Heber City being among the fastest-growing communities in Utah.

To help counteract the funding implications — state dollars follow students — the Board of Education has opened enrollment to out-of-boundary applicants for the 2027-2028 school year. Board President Meredith Reed told KPCW the district sees an opportunity to fill classrooms with kids who live elsewhere but want to attend Wasatch County schools. Superintendent Garrick Peterson told the board in October that the county's rising birth rate offers a longer-term reason for optimism.

Leaders note that the valley's growth story is complicated: Heber City unveiled six affordable homes in August and Midway approved its first affordable housing development in October, moves that could eventually bring younger families into the district. For now, though, school-age population has not kept pace with the broader housing boom.

events.description: A bronze memorial plaque honoring Lance Corporal Blaine A. Welch — the only Wasatch County service member killed in action during the Vietnam War — will be formally unveiled. The project was funded by a 5-0 City Council vote in April using TAP tax dollars.

events.title: Pro Skijor Frontier Tour — Soldier Hollow
events.description: Professional skijoring — where a horse and rider race alongside a skier through a course of gates, jumps, and obstacles — returns to the Wasatch Back as part of the 2027 Frontier Tour's second Utah stop. The tour also visits Salt Lake City on February 6.

moreNews.headline: Professional Skijoring Returning to Soldier Hollow in February
moreNews.body: The 2027 Frontier Tour announced November 5 that it will bring professional skijoring competition back to Soldier Hollow Nordic Center in Midway for February 26-28, 2027 — a new venue compared to past Heber City events. The sport pairs a horse and rider with a skier or snowboarder navigating a snow-packed obstacle course. The tour also includes a February 6 stop in Salt Lake City, plus new events in Denver and Lake Tahoe.
